paragraphs.ncert_ref: Structural Organisation in Animals: epithelial tissue
paragraphs.meaning: Epithelial tissue covers surfaces and lines cavities, and every epithelium has a free surface and a base resting on a basement membrane. Its cells are packed tightly with almost no space between them, which is what makes it a barrier. The shape of the cells and the number of layers decide its job: flat cells for exchange, cuboidal for secretion, columnar for absorption.

words.meaning: The thin layer under an epithelium that anchors it to the tissue below.
words.breakdown: It is non-cellular and made of proteins and glycoproteins.
words.trap: The basement membrane is not a cell layer. Calling it a membrane of cells confuses it with the plasma membrane.

words.meaning: A single layer of flat cells, found where diffusion must be easy.
words.breakdown: It lines the alveoli and blood vessels, and forms the skin's outer layer.
words.trap: Flat does not mean weak. Squamous cells are thin so gases cross quickly, which is the point.

words.meaning: A columnar cell that secretes mucus.
words.breakdown: Found in the lining of the intestine and respiratory tract.
words.trap: Goblet cells are unicellular glands within an epithelium, not a separate tissue.

paragraphs.visual_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 150'><path class='d-line' d='M40 56h240'/><path class='d-guide' d='M40 46h240'/><rect class='d-line' x='40' y='56' width='36' height='24'/><rect class='d-line' x='80' y='56' width='36' height='24'/><rect class='d-line' x='120' y='56' width='36' height='30'/><rect class='d-line' x='160' y='56' width='36' height='30'/><rect class='d-line' x='200' y='56' width='36' height='44'/><rect class='d-line' x='240' y='56' width='36' height='44'/><text class='d-label' x='40' y='40'>free surface</text><text class='d-label' x='40' y='104'>basement membrane</text><text class='d-label' x='40' y='132'>flat, cuboidal, then tall columnar</text></svg>
paragraphs.visual_alt: Epithelial cells drawn in a row, changing from flat to cuboidal to tall columnar, with the free surface and basement membrane labelled.
paragraphs.hook: The skin on your hand and the lining of your lung are the same kind of tissue doing two different jobs.
paragraphs.exam_note: Match structure to location: squamous in alveoli, cuboidal in kidney tubules, ciliated columnar in the respiratory tract.
paragraphs.trap: Cilia move mucus; microvilli increase surface area. They look similar in a diagram but do different jobs.

recall.q: The alveoli of the lungs are lined by
recall.why: Flat squamous cells give the thinnest barrier, which is what rapid gas exchange needs.

recall.q: Epithelial tissue is attached to the tissue below by
recall.why: The non-cellular basement membrane anchors the epithelium and separates it from the underlying connective tissue.

paragraphs.review_note: Verify page and line against your edition, and confirm the tissue examples in your printing.

paragraphs.ncert_ref: Structural Organisation in Animals: connective tissue
paragraphs.meaning: Connective tissue is defined by its matrix, not its cells: a few cells sit spread out in a large amount of material they secreted. The matrix decides the property, from the flexible gel of loose connective tissue to the hard calcium phosphate of bone. Blood is a connective tissue too, with a liquid matrix and cells floating in it.

words.meaning: The non-cellular material around connective tissue cells.
words.breakdown: It may be liquid as in blood, gel-like as in areolar tissue, or solid as in bone.
words.trap: The matrix is not empty space. It is secreted by the cells and carries the tissue's mechanical properties.

words.meaning: A cord of dense connective tissue joining muscle to bone.
words.breakdown: Tendons are strong and inelastic, made mostly of collagen fibres.
words.trap: A ligament joins bone to bone and is elastic. Swapping tendon and ligament is the commonest error in this section.

words.meaning: Loose connective tissue with cells packed with fat.
words.breakdown: It stores energy, cushions organs and insulates the body.
words.trap: Fat is not dead tissue. Adipose cells are living and take part in hormone signalling.

paragraphs.visual_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 150'><rect class='d-line' x='30' y='34' width='80' height='72' rx='2'/><circle class='d-fill' cx='52' cy='56' r='4'/><circle class='d-fill' cx='80' cy='80' r='4'/><path class='d-guide' d='M30 106h80'/><text class='d-label' x='30' y='126'>few cells</text><text class='d-label' x='126' y='52'>matrix</text><text class='d-label' x='126' y='70'>decides the property</text><path class='d-muted' d='M126 96c50 0 60 24 120 24'/><text class='d-label' x='126' y='140'>tendon to bone, ligament bone to bone</text></svg>
paragraphs.visual_alt: A connective tissue block with sparse cells in a large matrix, plus a note contrasting tendon and ligament.
paragraphs.hook: In most tissues the cells do the work. Here the material between them does.
paragraphs.exam_note: Questions test the tendon and ligament distinction, and the identity of blood as connective tissue. Both are reliable marks.
paragraphs.trap: Blood is connective tissue because of its plasma matrix, not a separate category. This appears in almost every paper.

recall.why: Ligaments join bone to bone and are elastic, while tendons join muscle to bone and are inelastic.

recall.q: Blood is classified as connective tissue because
recall.why: The defining feature of connective tissue is a matrix, and in blood that matrix is plasma.

paragraphs.review_note: Verify page and line against your edition, and check the tissue descriptions against your copy.

paragraphs.ncert_ref: Structural Organisation in Animals: muscle tissue
paragraphs.meaning: Muscle tissue contracts, and it comes in three forms. Skeletal muscle is striped, has many nuclei per cell and moves under conscious control. Smooth muscle is unstriped with single spindle-shaped cells and works without our will, while cardiac muscle is striped but involuntary and has intercalated discs, so heart cells contract as one unit.

words.meaning: Muscle with alternating light and dark bands visible under a microscope.
words.breakdown: Skeletal and cardiac muscle are striated; smooth muscle is not.
words.trap: Stripes do not mean voluntary. Cardiac muscle is striated and involuntary, which breaks the simple rule.

words.meaning: The junction between adjacent cardiac muscle cells.
words.breakdown: It lets electrical signals pass quickly from cell to cell.
words.trap: Intercalated discs are found only in cardiac muscle. They are not part of skeletal muscle.

words.meaning: Unstriped, involuntary muscle in the walls of hollow organs.
words.breakdown: Found in the stomach, intestine, blood vessels and bladder.
words.trap: Smooth muscle cells are spindle-shaped and single-nucleated, unlike the long multinucleate skeletal fibres.

paragraphs.visual_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 150'><rect class='d-line' x='26' y='40' width='90' height='30' rx='2'/><path class='d-muted' d='M30 50h82M30 60h82'/><path class='d-accent' d='M30 50h82'/><path class='d-line' d='M26 96h90'/><path class='d-accent' d='M40 96c0-18 20-18 20 0M70 96c0-18 20-18 20 0M100 96c0-18 16-18 16 0'/><rect class='d-line' x='190' y='40' width='90' height='30' rx='2'/><path class='d-guide' d='M232 40v30'/><text class='d-label' x='26' y='86'>skeletal: striped, many nuclei</text><text class='d-label' x='26' y='132'>smooth: unstriped, spindle cells</text><text class='d-label' x='190' y='86'>cardiac: striped, discs</text></svg>
paragraphs.visual_alt: Skeletal, smooth and cardiac muscle drawn in three rows, each labelled with its distinguishing feature.
paragraphs.hook: Your heart is striped like a leg muscle, and you still cannot tell it to stop.
paragraphs.exam_note: Cardiac muscle is the exception that appears in every paper: striated but involuntary, with intercalated discs.
paragraphs.trap: Skeletal muscle fibres are multinucleate, not single-nucleate. That is one of the standard distinguishing points.

recall.why: It shows stripes like skeletal muscle but is not under conscious control, and its cells are joined by intercalated discs.
They join cardiac muscle cells so that the heart contracts as a coordinated unit.

paragraphs.ncert_ref: Structural Organisation in Animals: neural tissue
paragraphs.meaning: Nervous tissue is built of neurons, which carry electrical signals, and glial cells, which support and insulate them. A neuron has a cell body, dendrites that receive signals and an axon that carries them away. Many axons are wrapped in myelin, which speeds conduction and gives white matter its colour.

words.meaning: The long process of a neuron that carries impulses away from the cell body.
words.breakdown: It ends in terminals that pass the signal to the next cell.
words.trap: Dendrites carry signals towards the cell body. Reversing the two is the standard slip.

words.meaning: A fatty insulating layer around many axons.
words.breakdown: Formed by Schwann cells outside the brain, and it speeds up conduction.
words.trap: Myelin does not carry the signal. It insulates the axon so the signal jumps between gaps.

words.meaning: Supporting cells of nervous tissue that do not conduct impulses themselves.
words.breakdown: They supply nutrients, remove waste and insulate neurons.
words.trap: Glial cells are not neurons. They outnumber neurons but do not fire action potentials in the same way.

paragraphs.visual_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 150'><circle class='d-line' cx='76' cy='74' r='16'/><path class='d-accent' d='M60 62l-20-14M58 74H34M60 86l-18 14'/><path class='d-accent' d='M92 74h120'/><path class='d-muted' d='M104 66h24M136 66h24M168 66h24'/><path class='d-accent' d='M212 68l16 6-16 6'/><text class='d-label' x='26' y='34'>dendrites in</text><text class='d-label' x='196' y='46'>axon out</text><text class='d-label' x='104' y='120'>myelin wraps the axon</text></svg>
paragraphs.visual_alt: A neuron with dendrites receiving on the left, an axon leaving right and myelin segments along it.
paragraphs.hook: Signals arrive on many branches and leave on one cable.
paragraphs.exam_note: Label a neuron correctly: dendrite, cell body, axon, myelin, terminal. Direction of impulse is a favourite question.
paragraphs.trap: An impulse travels from dendrite to axon, never the other way in a normal neuron. Synapses are one-way junctions.

recall.q: Impulses travel along a neuron from
recall.why: Dendrites receive and the axon carries the impulse away towards the next cell, which makes the junction one-way.
Myelin insulates the axon, so the impulse jumps between the gaps and travels faster.
